437:
However, we couldn’t check it:
Prokhorov didn’t show up for the meeting.
438:
He likely suspected something. Quit his job,
didn’t come home.
440:
And to you—our deepest apologies, immense thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home, celebrate the New Year. Thank you very much.
- And my guys?
442: We’ll return your wards to their place today.
443:
And if the coat-check guy turns up,
we might need you again?
444: I didn’t want to tell you, but today Bely—the Docent—escaped from the colony.
445: Unbelievable, but true. For you to stay like this is dangerous.
446: Maybe tomorrow? It’s New Year’s, after all, and they did try in their own way.
447: We live out of town—unlikely the Docent can find us.
448:
All right—only don’t step off the dacha grounds!
Also, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev’s wife—here’s her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You’ll have lunch with us on the first—promise?
- We promise!
451: Shame—such a good woman, and her father’s a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you out?
- He showed up... a bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this new year,
everything for you will be new.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
and I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one moment...
- Where’d he go?
458: Who knows? You can’t understand anything with him now.
459:
What’s there to understand? “Wherever you are,” he says,
“I’ll find you and slit your throat.”
461:
They say he did Ryaboy with a razor—snip, and bye-bye.
- Totally went rabid, the jackal.
462:
Who’s come to you? Santa Claus has come to you,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come, come. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don’t even have a home.
- You will. It’s all ahead.
465:
- For now they’ll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you know is to croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- What, you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471: We could just sit and talk heart-to-heart.
472:
I’m not a prosecutor to talk heart-to-heart with you.
- We could play something.
473:
Would you look at that! Found a sucker to play with you!
You’ve got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here’s a good game—cities.
I say “Moscow,”
476:
and you, on the last letter “A”—Astrakhan.
Then you, on “N”—Novgorod, get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Okay. Then you—on “A.”
- Jambul. - What’s Jambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it’s warm there, that’s my home,
that’s my mom.
481:
Then let’s play this way. I’ll go out, you hide something,
I come back—I find it.
482:
- You’d better find our helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We’ll hide it, and he’ll peek through a crack?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don’t peek.
Why me? Anything happens—right away it’s Fedya.
485:
- I’ll rip your mouth open, you little bastard!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- You had a dad and mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so angry? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on your own.
- Ah, you’re here too.
491:
I started to come to you, but I feel—
it’s an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need to hide out.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It’s fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499: “Hello, dear Dad! We found out you’re in prison,
500: and we were very happy, because we thought you were dead.”
501: What scumbag told that little punk about Dweeb?
502: “And Mom was happy too, because when the letter came, she cried all day,
503: and before that she said you were a test pilot.”
505: “And I’m happy anyway that you’re alive, because Mom says
507: Exactly! Weak-willed—stole the shared money and blamed the cabbie.
508: Beat it! I’ll knock your horns off, you radish!
510:
Shame on you! You’re 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What’s behind you? What’s in the present?
What’s ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it’s too late. That’s my advice.
513:
Hey, Docent, we gotta take off:
The lady doctor will rat to the police.
514:
- She won’t. - Why?
- I did her with the razor across the throat...
515: she’s in the well—go take a look.
516: How much did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and apartment?
Let’s say ten!
520: And for a lousy 14 years I’m supposed to put up with this viper?
521:
The one the old woman dumped in the well?
Do what you want, I’m going to the police.
523:
And you? You’ll keep putting up with him
until you die, yeah?
524: Vas, I told him earlier: I’ve got a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough—your runny nose is getting old.
Come here...
527:
- What’re you up to?
- We’re gonna beat a carpet.
528:
All right, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I’m taking this off.
530:
I’ll do my time and that’s it. I’ll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A guard at your native collective farm.
- Why a guard?
532: I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we brought the cap too!
Who’s the Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but only one cap.
- If we had the helmet, they’d cut our time.
535: Where’d he put it? We searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I’ve got a runny nose?
And you: “Mouth, mouth.”
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538: When we got busted. Remember? He says, I’m fishing, and you dive.
539:
- Wait—what did he say about fishing then?
- He said, I’m fishing in an ice hole,
540:
- and you, Cross-Eyed, know how to swim?
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that’s what!
541:
Exactly! I remember, that bad person!
In the ice hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn’t you say so, you lout? Could’ve left a note before hanging yourself.
- Let’s go.
543:
- And him?
- Forget it—let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let’s go!
545:
- There’s nothing there.
- It’s there, on the bottom. Need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away it’s Cross-Eyed.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can’t! It’s cold—I’ll get sick.
548:
- Just tried to hang himself, now he’s afraid of catching cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where’s the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I’d stitch you up, but I don’t have time to fuss with you!
552:
Now it’s two pieces.
And there’s another one at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
